Algebraic reasoning: Point A(-3, 2) is on the reciprocal function y2=m/x, so m=(-3)·2=-6, therefore y2=-6/x. Point B(n, -3/2) is also on y2=-6/x, so -3/2=-6/n, solving gives n=4, that is B(4, -3/2). The straight line y1=kx+b passes through A(-3,2) and B(4,-3/2), and the slope k=[-3/2-2]/[4-(-3)]=(-7/2)/7=-1/2. Substitute point A: 2=(-1/2)(-3)+b=3/2+b, obtaining b=1/2, so y1=-x/2+1/2.

It is required that y1>y2, that is -x/2+1/2>-6/x, and x≠0. Moving terms gives -x/2+1/2+6/x>0, reducing to a common denominator gives [-(x-4)(x+3)]/(2x)>0. The critical points are x=-3, 0, 4. By making a sign analysis, the intervals on which the inequality holds are x<-3 or 0<x<4.

Final answer: x∈(-∞,-3)∪(0,4).
